articles.title: Why Does a Wool Jumper Keep You Warm?
articles.dek: The secret is not in the sheep. It is in the air!

sources.name: Science Learning Hub – Wool fibre properties
The Woolmark Company – Wool is naturally breathable

paras: It is the coldest month of the year. You open your wardrobe. What do you choose: a cotton T-shirt or a wool jumper? Most people choose the wool jumper. But why is wool so warm? The answer is in the tiny hairs of a sheep.

Wool comes from sheep. Every hair of wool is very thin, but it is not straight. It has lots of small waves, like a curly line. Scientists call these waves crimp. Because of the crimp, the hairs cannot lie flat next to each other. So there are lots of small spaces between them.

These spaces are full of air. Air does not move heat well. So the air in your jumper keeps the warmth from your body near your skin. The cold air outside cannot get in easily. This is the most important reason why wool keeps you warm.

Wool has another clever trick. It can hold a lot of water, up to about 30 percent of its own weight. But it still doesn't feel wet. On a rainy walk, a wet cotton T-shirt feels cold and heavy. A wool jumper is not as cold as cotton when it gets a little wet.

Wool is good in other ways too. It does not burn easily, so it is a good material for blankets and carpets. It is natural, and it grows back after a farmer cuts it. But some people think wool feels itchy. The softest wool comes from merino sheep, because their hairs are the thinnest.
So which jumper is the best for a snowy day? A wool one is a great choice. Wear a thin wool layer under your coat, and you will be as warm as a sheep in a field!

articles.title: Grandma's First Smartphone
articles.dek: Grandma Ingrid couldn't send a message. Then Lucas gave her some lessons.
paras: Hi everyone, it's Lucas again! This month my blog is about my grandma, Ingrid. She is seventy-four, and she is amazing. She can make the best apple cake in town. But until last month, she couldn't use a smartphone. She only had an old phone with big buttons.

When Grandma was young, life was very different. She told me about it on Sunday. "I couldn't phone my friends from my bedroom," she said. "We had one phone in the hall. My brother always used it!" But she could ride a horse, and she could swim across the lake near her village.

On her birthday, Mum gave her a smartphone. Grandma looked at it for a long time. "What a beautiful little screen," she said. "But I can't read these tiny letters!" So I made the letters bigger for her. Then I showed her the camera.

Every Saturday after that, I gave her a lesson at her kitchen table. In the first week, she could send a text message, but it took ten minutes. In the second week, she learned to take photos. Most of them were photos of her own finger! We laughed a lot.

Now Grandma can do lots of things on her phone. She can make video calls to my cousin in Canada. She can look up recipes online. Yesterday she sent me a message with three hearts and a cake. She can't play games yet, but she wants to learn.
I think teaching Grandma was the most fun job of my year. She taught me something too: you can learn new things at any age. Has anyone in your family got a new gadget? Tell me in the comments!

articles.title: Welcome to Our Home, Ana!
articles.dek: Ana is going to stay with a family in England. What are the house rules?
paras: Ana is fourteen and lives in Brazil. Next month, she is staying with a family in England for two weeks. Read her emails with Mrs Clarke.

Hi Ana, We are very happy that you are coming! Here is some information about our home. You don't have to bring towels or sheets, because we have lots. But you must bring warm clothes. It is very cold here in December. Our house is small, so you have to share a bedroom with our daughter, Lily. She is fourteen too, and she is very excited.

On school days, we have breakfast at seven o'clock. You have to be ready by half past seven, because the school bus leaves at twenty to eight. After school, you don't have to help in the kitchen, but you can if you want! At the weekend, we get up late. Best wishes, Helen Clarke

Dear Mrs Clarke, Thank you for your email. I'm excited too! I have some questions. At home in Brazil, I play the guitar every evening. Can I bring my guitar? Do I have to practise in my room? And must I wear a uniform at Lily's school? We don't have to wear one at my school. Love, Ana

Hi Ana, Of course you can bring your guitar! Lily plays the piano, so you can play music together. You can practise in the living room, but you have to stop at nine o'clock. Our neighbour has a new baby. And yes, you must wear a uniform at school. Don't worry, we have one for you. It's dark blue.
Oh, one more thing. In our house, everyone must take their shoes off at the door. We have a white carpet! See you very soon, Helen

items.why: Questions with have to start with Do / Does.

items.q: Lily ___ share her bedroom next month.
items.why: Lily = she, so have becomes has: has to.

items.q: Ana ___ cook dinner. Mrs Clarke always cooks it.
items.a: doesn't have to / does not have to
items.why: It is not necessary, and Ana = she: doesn't have to.

items.q: You ___ be quiet after nine o'clock. The baby next door is sleeping.
items.why: It is necessary to be quiet, so use must.

kps.fact: Ana is going to stay with a family in England for two weeks.
kps.q: How long is Ana staying in England?

kps.fact: Ana must bring warm clothes, but she doesn't have to bring towels.
kps.q: What does Ana NOT have to bring?

kps.fact: The school bus leaves at twenty to eight.
kps.q: When does the school bus leave?

kps.fact: Ana can practise the guitar in the living room until nine o'clock.
kps.q: When does Ana have to stop playing?

kps.fact: Everyone must take their shoes off at the door.
kps.q: Where must everyone take their shoes off?

mindmap.question: What does Ana need to know about her stay?

summary.intro: Choose the three sentences that tell the main ideas of the emails.
summary.model: Ana is staying with the Clarkes in England, so Mrs Clarke tells her the house rules. Ana can bring her guitar, but she must take her shoes off.

options.t: Mrs Clarke tells Ana what to bring and about school days.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 2 and 3.
options.evidence: Here is some information about our home.

options.t: Ana asks about her guitar and a school uniform.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraph 4.

options.t: Ana can bring her guitar, but there are some rules.
options.why: This is the main idea of paragraphs 5 and 6.
options.evidence: Of course you can bring your guitar!

options.t: The Clarkes' neighbour has a new baby.
options.why: True, but it is only a small detail.
options.evidence: Our neighbour has a new baby.

options.t: Ana is going to fly to England with her mum.
Ana has her own bedroom in the house.
options.why: Wrong: she has to share a bedroom with Lily.
options.evidence: Our house is small, so you have to share a bedroom with our daughter, Lily.

speak.p: What rules are there in your home? Which rule do you like, and which one don't you like? Why?
speak.hint: At home I have to … / I don't have to …, because …

write.p: A friend from another country is coming to stay at your home. Write an email to your friend. Write 25 words or more.
steps: Say what your friend must bring.
Say what your friend doesn't have to bring.
Say one rule in your home.
